messages:
sara: Quick intake — I sketched a launch decision rubric for the new per-route QoS feature. Want to validate acceptance criteria and edge cases before I turn into a PRD.

devon: thanks, can you paste the high-level problem + proposed success metrics? helps me think about infra implications.

sara: problem: customers want per-route QoS (latency/cost prioritization) so platform can route high-value requests to low-latency paths without manual config per model.

olivia: goals from product/design perspective:
- clear success metric: 95th percentile tail latency for 'high' routes <= 120ms at 95% of traffic for Tier-1 customers
- measurable cost delta: per-token cost uplift <= 15% for high QoS vs baseline
- UX: route create flow in console < 2 min for common templates

mike: non-goals: not solving multi-tenant noisy neighbor isolation here; that's a separate infra project. also not handling arbitrary per-request model selection logic.

ash: acceptance criteria (proposal):
- API: POST /routes accepts qos_profile enum (low/standard/high) and validates falls back to default
- Routing: traffic tagged high is routed to low-latency pool or compatible model variant; fallback policy defined
- Observability: dashboard shows per-route latency P50/P95/P99 and per-token cost. Alerts fire when P95>120ms for 10m
- Rollout: canary to 5% traffic, automated rollback if success metrics degrade by >5% vs baseline

devon: infra notes: need to surface route affinity in router, plus quota accounting by route. also require a quantization-aware variant for low-latency pool.

sara: edge cases I think we should call out:
- Route targets a model with incompatible sequence length / unsupported ops — should auto-fallback and log a warning (no silent failure)
- Mixed traffic: single customer route with both streaming and non-streaming requests — ensure streaming SLOs preserved
- Sudden burst on high routes — autoscale policy should allow short burst up to 2x reserved capacity before throttling
- Billing: if fallback occurs, invoices must show which requests were served by fallback variant

mike: +1 on explicit billing tags. also: KV cache affinity — if high route hits a different pool, cold cache penalty could spike latency. need to measure warmup effect and include in canary checks.

olivia: UX edgecases: when creating a route, if selected model isn't available in low-latency pool, console should show recommended compatible variants and a one-click 'create fallback variant' flow.

sara: proposed rollout decision rubric (quick):
- Beta: internal + 3 customers, must meet latency and cost targets for 72h under real traffic
- GA: Beta success + automated observability + billing transparency + documented failure modes
- Blockers: inability to reliably route >95% of high-tagged requests to low-latency pool, or >15% cost overshoot for >24h

devon: operational acceptance: we also need a playbook entry for fallback events and a synthetic test job that hits per-route SLOs every 5m.

ash: next steps: sara to update PRD with the rubric, add a small acceptance checklist for eng and SRE, olivia to wire mockups for the console fallback UX. mike/devon to estimate infra work for quantized variant and router changes.

sara: thanks — I'll turn this into a PRD draft today and ping for quick review. tagging @deploy-bot: please run a short thread reminder in 48h if not merged. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: reminder scheduled: will ping #product in 48 hours.
